title: Quantified Model Portfolio & Scouting Playbook
creator: Leah Ortega
description:
Objective:
Create a repeatable, quantitative playbook for discovering, scoring, and translating signals from the open model landscape into prioritized provisioning and commercial sourcing actions for Redwood customers. The output is a scorecard + cadence + automated alerts that map model signals to recommended actions (add to catalog, onboard variant, provision Dedicated capacity, or flag for legal).

Scope:
- Focus on models relevant to text-generation and embeddings initially (expand to multimodal later).
- Inputs: public model releases, internal benchmark runs, customer telemetry (latency/cost/quality), license/terms metadata, third-party provider notices.
- Outputs: model portfolio CSV, weekly digest, rolling "procurement trigger" alert set, one-page sourcing playbook, and integration hooks for the Console's model catalog.

Success metrics:
- Coverage: new model candidates captured within 7 days of first public release (target 85%).
- False positive rate for procurement triggers < 15% after first two quarters.
- Time-to-action from trigger to provisioning decision < 10 business days for P0/P1 triggers.

Scoring rubric (initial draft):
- Quality (0-30): weighted evals on task battery (summarization, instruction-following, safety benchmarks).
- Cost Efficiency (0-20): measured tokens-per-dollar on standard prompts under Redwood runtime.
- Latency & Resource Footprint (0-15): median tail latency on standard sequences + VRAM footprint/quantization friendliness.
- Operational Compatibility (0-15): ease of integration (ONNX/pt, kv cache compatibility, required custom kernels).
- Legal/Risk (0-10): license risk, export controls, provenance.
- Ecosystem Signals (0-10): community uptake, official maintainer cadence, packaged tooling.

Each model receives a composite score and a band: "Experiment", "Candidate for Catalog", "Provision if demand > X", "Enterprise-risk (block)". The playbook will include threshold maps to convert score + telemetry to a recommended action.

Data flows and automation:
- Ingest: RSS/GitHub monitor + curated vendor feeds -> candidate queue in Confluence sheet.
- Bench pipeline: nightly sandbox runs (ENG-54812) produce eval CSVs.
- Telemetry join: link candidate with customer traffic signals (Console usage, latency, error rates).
- Alerting: if composite score delta >= 7 points or customer-interest signal > 250 API calls/week, generate a procurement trigger to the PM on-call.

Operational playbook steps (first 30 days):
1) Triage candidate -> owner assignment -> quick license check.
2) Run lightweight eval suite (5 prompts each category) -> compute provisional score.
3) If provisional score >= 60 -> schedule full benchmark + cost run (2x larger suite).
4) If telemetry shows interest (customer mentions, early calls) -> escalate to provisioning review with Solutions Eng.
5) Document decision and update model catalog entry with provenance, chosen quantization, and recommended routing policy.

Deliverables:
- PM-owned Confluence playbook (one-pager + rubric) + CSV template.
- Weekly digest email template & initial automation (via webhook).
- Prototype dashboard (Grafana) that surfaces top delta models and triggers.
- Integration spec for Console model catalog (small PR).

Risks & mitigations:
- Bench capacity limits: schedule low-cost subsample runs and prioritize by upstream signal. (Mitigation: ENG backlog item ENG-54812 to increase ephemeral benches.)
- License ambiguity: route ambiguous licenses to Legal immediately; add a temporary "Hold" band to the catalog.
- Noise in telemetry: require signal smoothing and multi-week confirmation before provisioning.

Next steps (owners):
- PM: finalize rubric and thresholds (Leah Ortega) by 2026-03-04.
- Eng: wire the nightly bench pipeline to the Confluence candidate sheet (ENG-54812).
- Data: provide mapping from Console usage to candidate entries (Data team ticket created).
